reply_text:
I found one possible 2019 prediction, and it still needs checking against the film. In the documentary *iHuman*, Sutskever gives a wide range for when human-level AI arrives. I have no direct quote with a date from any other 2019 occasion, and nothing was already recorded for this year.

**The candidate.** A quote collection on dailydoc.com, with timestamps, attributes this to Sutskever at 59:07–59:14 of *iHuman*: "We haven't created the human-level thinking machine yet, but we get closer and closer. Maybe we'll get to human-level AI in 5 years from now, or maybe it'll take 50 or 100 years from now—it almost doesn't matter."

Three caveats:
- **I could not confirm the words in a transcript.** The transcript page I opened (scrapsfromtheloft.com) cut off before that point in the film. It also doesn't name speakers. The only page that carries the words is a third-party write-up, so I marked it coverage_only. Someone should watch the film at about 59:07.
- **The date is uncertain.** The film premiered at the IDFA festival in Amsterdam (Wikipedia gives 23 November 2019). I don't know when the interview was filmed, so it might come from an earlier year.
- **It may not count as a forecast.** The span runs from 5 to 100 years, and he says the timing "almost doesn't matter." It's up to you whether that counts.

**A line I couldn't attribute.** In the transcript, right after a passage that the dailydoc page attributes to Sutskever, someone says "You're gonna see dramatically more intelligent systems in 10 or 15 years from now…". The transcript doesn't say who is speaking, and dailydoc's version of his quote stops just before this line. I left it out, but checking the film around 15:39 would settle it.

**Other 2019 occasions I checked:**
- **His VB Transform talk with Greg Brockman (July 2019):** the only page I opened was someone's summary notes. They describe his hopes for reasoning but give no dates and no exact quotes.
- **His ScaledML talk on GPT-2 (March 2019):** I found a YouTube recording but no transcript, and I didn't watch it.
- **The New Yorker article "The Next Word" (October 2019):** the copy I opened held only the start of the page and none of his words, and the gwern.net page I opened was cut off before his quotes.
- **Lex Fridman podcast #94:** this was recorded in 2020, so it belongs to another year.

I used 11 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings. My first code run crashed while printing the results of the first search, but the search ran only once and I used its saved results.
